issues.description: Class member: Bitmap24 default (no-argument) constructor. Template repository's header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) does NOT declare a default constructor; the implementation file (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) DEFINES Bitmap24::Bitmap24() and main.cpp (example_program/src/main.cpp) instantiates Bitmap24 using the default constructor. The solution repository's header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) DECLARES the default constructor. This mismatch (header vs implementation vs usage) causes compilation/linkage errors for students: main.cpp expects a declared default constructor but the template header omits it even though it is defined in the .cpp file.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a declaration for the default constructor to the template header to match the implementation and usage. In example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp, add the line 'Bitmap24();' (matching the solution header) so that the class declares the no-argument constructor present in Bitmap24.cpp and used in main.cpp. Ensure the declaration signature exactly matches the implementation (no arguments) and keep the existing parameterized constructor and destructor declarations.
